grammar_note_en: você takes 3rd-person singular verb forms in PT-BR

examples.en_sentence: Do you have a phone here?

grammar_note_en: a gente means 'we' in spoken PT-BR and takes 3rd-person singular verbs

examples.en_sentence: We are going to eat today.

grammar_note_en: não goes directly before the verb

examples.en_sentence: I do not want coffee now.
She is not going to speak today.

grammar_note_en: ser is used for identity, origin, and permanent traits

examples.en_sentence: Everything is going to be perfect today.
He wants to have an apartment.
She wants to see a movie.
Are you going to want a coffee?
We are going to do everything.

grammar_note_en: ir + infinitive forms the near future ('going to')

examples.en_sentence: I am going to eat now.
Maria is going to speak today.

grammar_note_en: precisar + infinitive (no preposition); precisar + de before nouns

examples.en_sentence: You are going to need to go today.
I am eating a lot today.
Ana is going to speak here.
I am not going to speak today.

grammar_note_en: muito is invariant before adjectives/verbs, but agrees in gender/number before nouns

examples.en_sentence: João is a very strong man.
You need to do everything now.

grammar_note_en: o (masc sg), a (fem sg), os (masc pl), as (fem pl)

examples.en_sentence: I want to see the movie.

grammar_note_en: de + o = do, de + a = da; precisar takes 'de' before nouns
no = em + o (in/at the, masc); na = em + a (in/at the, fem)

examples.en_sentence: We are eating at the restaurant today.
I see Ana in the photo.
He is going to eat at a hotel.

grammar_note_en: estar is used for location and temporary states (often shortened to tô/tá in speech)

examples.en_sentence: I am at the hotel now.
Maria is at the hospital today.
I want to be here today.

grammar_note_en: Often pronounced 'pra' in everyday spoken PT-BR

examples.en_sentence: I am going to Brazil today.
I am going to talk with Maria.
We are eating with João today.

grammar_note_en: Use 'o que' at the start of questions for 'what'

examples.en_sentence: What do you want to eat?
She says that everything is perfect.

grammar_note_en: Use 'bem' with estar (estou bem = I am fine) and verbs
Do not confuse 'mas' (but) with 'mais' (more)

examples.en_sentence: I want to go but I am not going.
He talks a lot but does not go.
The plan is simple but perfect.
Ana and João are at the hotel.
I want coffee and music now.
The restaurant is simple and perfect.

grammar_note_en: um (masc sg), uma (fem sg)
Agrees with the noun: meu carro (masc), minha família (fem)

examples.en_sentence: Do you see my phone here?

grammar_note_en: Agrees with the noun: seu plano (masc), sua foto (fem)
In spoken PT-BR, 'isso' covers both 'this' and 'that' for abstract ideas

examples.en_sentence: I do not want to do that.
We need to talk about that.

grammar_note_en: 'em casa' = at home (no article); 'na casa' = in the house

examples.en_sentence: I do not have time now.
I will be able to eat at home.

grammar_note_en: Use 'saber' for facts and skills (not people or places)

examples.en_sentence: I do not know how to do that.
Do you know the plan today?
She needs to know about everything.
I have a thing for you.
We are doing many things today.
I give the coffee to you.
She hands the photo to Maria.
I am staying at home today.
João is staying at the hotel now.

grammar_note_en: lá refers to a place far from both speaker and listener

examples.en_sentence: I am going to eat there today.
The restaurant is over there in Brazil.

grammar_note_en: dia is masculine despite ending in -a (um dia, o dia)

examples.en_sentence: I am staying there for many days.

grammar_note_en: Use 'bom/boa' with nouns (um bom dia), 'bem' with verbs (estou bem)
Do not confuse 'mais' (more) with 'mas' (but)

examples.en_sentence: When is he going to talk with me?
I do not know when I am going.
Who do you want to talk with?

grammar_note_en: 'porque' (one word) means 'because' in answers and explanations

examples.en_sentence: I am staying because I am fine here.
She eats because she has time.
I am not going because I need to stay.

grammar_note_en: por + o = pelo, por + a = pela; used for routes, exchanges, and 'por aqui'

examples.en_sentence: I do this for your sake.

grammar_note_en: PT-BR uses double negatives: 'não quero nada' (I don't want anything)

examples.en_sentence: I do not want anything now.

en_gloss: to grab / to pick up / to take

examples.en_sentence: I am grabbing my car now.
Ana picks up the coffee here.

grammar_note_en: gostar always takes 'de' before its object (gostar de + noun/verb)

examples.en_sentence: You are going to like the movie.
He is not saying anything today.

grammar_note_en: 'o cara' (masc) = the guy/dude; 'a cara' (fem) = the face

examples.en_sentence: The guy is at the restaurant.
Who is the guy over there?

grammar_note_en: 'de noite' or 'à noite' = at night

examples.en_sentence: I stay at home at night.
I have a lot of work today.
I do not have money now.

grammar_note_en: amigo (male friend), amiga (female friend)

examples.en_sentence: I am going to talk with my friend.

grammar_note_en: Do not confuse 'vir' (to come) with 'ver' (to see)
'Eu acho que...' is the everyday PT-BR way to say 'I think that...'

examples.en_sentence: What do you think of that?
I need to find my phone.

grammar_note_en: Use 'sair de' for leaving a place (sair de casa = leave home)

examples.en_sentence: We are going to go out at night.

grammar_note_en: 'Que horas são?' = What time is it? 'na hora' = on time / right away

examples.en_sentence: Now is the time to leave.
I am staying there for one hour.

grammar_note_en: Very common in spoken PT-BR for 'cool / nice' (same form for masc and fem)

examples.en_sentence: What a cool idea you have!

grammar_note_en: 'ainda não' = not yet

examples.en_sentence: She does not know that yet.
Do you still want to eat here?

grammar_note_en: Use 'depois de' before a noun or infinitive

examples.en_sentence: I am going to eat later.

grammar_note_en: 'por que' (two words) is used to ask 'why?' in questions

examples.en_sentence: Why are you not coming today?
Why do we need to leave?

grammar_note_en: aí refers to a place near the listener, or 'then' in spoken stories
Use 'conhecer' for people, places, and things (not facts)

examples.en_sentence: She wants to meet your family.

grammar_note_en: 'mal' is the opposite of 'bem' (estou mal = I feel unwell)

examples.en_sentence: He speaks very badly of that.
Ana is doing badly at the hospital.

grammar_note_en: Use 'pedir' to request/order something (not to ask a question)

examples.en_sentence: I am ordering a coffee now.
He always asks for more time.
We are going to order coffee.

grammar_note_en: Use 'morar em' for where someone resides

examples.en_sentence: Do you want to live here?
I am looking at the photo now.
Can you look at this here?

grammar_note_en: Use 'deixar' when leaving an object behind (not 'sair')

examples.en_sentence: I am going back home now.
He is coming back from work today.
We are going to come back later.

grammar_note_en: 'uma vez' = once; 'muitas vezes' = many times / often

examples.en_sentence: I am working at home today.
João works at the local hospital.
She needs to work at night.
Ana buys water at the restaurant.
We want to buy a car.
I am drinking a lot of water today.
He does not drink coffee at night.
Do you want to drink water now?

grammar_note_en: Note the stem change in 1st person singular: eu durmo

examples.en_sentence: I am going to work tomorrow.
He is coming back from the hotel tomorrow.
I live in the city now.
Do you know the city well?

grammar_note_en: 'de novo' = again

examples.en_sentence: She lives in a new house.

grammar_note_en: Same form for masculine and feminine singular
Use 'perguntar' to ask a question (not 'pedir')
viver = to live/experience life (whereas morar = to reside at an address)
aquilo refers to an abstract or unidentified thing far from both speakers

examples.en_sentence: I do not want to see that.
That over there is not normal.

grammar_note_en: False friend: 'pais' (no accent) = parents; 'país' (with accent) = country

examples.en_sentence: I am going to talk with my parents.
Are your parents in the city?

grammar_note_en: False friend: 'assistir' means 'to watch' (not to assist/help)

examples.en_sentence: I am watching the movie today.
We are going to watch a movie.

grammar_note_en: Use 'levar' for taking someone/something away from here

examples.en_sentence: I am taking my car tomorrow.
Can you take water over there?
I need to tell you something.
